clue.text: In need of make-up

parts.note: make-up reads as cosmetics, but here it is a shortfall that has to be made up

explanation.surface: Someone without their cosmetics feels they badly need a touch-up.
explanation.definitionFit: A deficit has to be made up, and something lacking what it should have is short of the required amount.

clue.text: It's a game, taking up the violin !

indicators.note: in a down clue, taking a word up means writing it from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a Strad is a Stradivarius, the most famous violin

explanation.surface: Someone takes up the fiddle as a pastime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking up' sounds like learning an instrument, but it turns STRAD upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A pub pastime of throwing arrows at a board.

clue.text: Heard or consumed at a Pop Festival ?

definitions.text: Heard or consumed at a Pop Festival

parts.words: Heard or consumed at a Pop Festival
parts.note: the trumpet flourish is heard; split in two it is food eaten by music lovers

explanation.surface: Something you hear or eat at a rock concert.
explanation.walkthrough: As one word it is a trumpet flourish; split as 'fan fare' it is what the fans eat.
explanation.definitionFit: A flourish of trumpets; also, as two words, the food fans eat.

clue.text: Where one is opposed to seven

definitions.text: Where one is opposed to seven

parts.words: Where one is opposed to seven
parts.note: the numerals 1 and 7 sit opposite each other on a dial

explanation.surface: Somewhere a single person fights against seven others.
explanation.definitionFit: On the dial of a timepiece the numeral 1 sits directly across from 7.

clue.text: 5s for those in distress, perhaps

explanation.surface: A cross-reference to tips for people in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 5 down is TIP, so '5s' are tips, the furthest points; extremity also means dire need.
explanation.definitionFit: Tips are the far ends of things, and extremity also means a state of great hardship.

clue.text: A hint for rubbish disposal

explanation.surface: Advice on getting rid of garbage.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a rubbish tip is a refuse dump.
explanation.definitionFit: A useful suggestion, and a British word for a waste dump.

clue.text: Make a clean sweep

parts.note: a clean sweep suggests a total victory, but read literally it is cleaning up with a mop

explanation.surface: A winner takes every prize on offer.
explanation.definitionFit: To finish off or clear away completely, as with spilt liquid wiped from a floor.

clue.text: A bigger agenda, say, for the feeble-minded ?

definitions.note: here a stand-in for one dim person, a noun like the answer

indicators.note: say tells us to speak the words and listen to the result

parts.note: a bigger agenda has more items on it, said as 'more on'

explanation.surface: A larger list of meeting items is suitable for dimwits.
explanation.definitionFit: An insulting term for a stupid person.

clue.text: Did she put the lid on hope?

definitions.text: Did she put the lid on hope?

parts.words: Did she put the lid on hope?
parts.note: in Greek myth the first woman shut her jar of evils with only hope left inside

explanation.surface: A question whether a woman crushed optimism.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put the lid on' sounds like ending hope, but in the myth she literally closed the jar, trapping hope inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The first woman of Greek myth, who released the world's ills from a jar.

clue.text: Fairylike arrangement of columns

explanation.surface: A delicate, dainty row of pillars.
explanation.walkthrough: A peri is a fairy of Persian myth, so 'peri-style' is fairylike; the real word is a colonnade round a court.
explanation.definitionFit: A ring of columns around a building or courtyard; split up it means in the manner of a Persian fairy.

clue.text: Tennysonian advice for the old

parts.note: Tennyson's In Memoriam bids the bells to dismiss the old year and welcome the new

explanation.surface: A Victorian poet counsels elderly people.
explanation.walkthrough: Tennyson's line is 'Ring out the old, ring in the new', so 'the old' is the past year, not old people.
explanation.definitionFit: Bells sound to bid farewell to the passing year in Tennyson's famous New Year poem.

clue.text: He's not alone in business or crime

definitions.text: He's not alone in business or crime

parts.words: He's not alone in business or crime
parts.note: both a firm and a robbery can be run by two people sharing the work

explanation.surface: A man always has an accomplice, at work or on a heist.
explanation.definitionFit: An associate shares a firm, and the idiom 'in crime' gives an accomplice.

clue.text: A blow for fishing

explanation.surface: Someone takes a swipe at an angler.
explanation.definitionFit: A slap is a sharp hit; a single-masted sailing boat used by fishermen has the same name.

clue.text: Wrong way to rouse Nero

indicators.note: a way of setting these words out means rearranging their letters into a new order

explanation.surface: Waking the emperor Nero this way is a mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'way' signals the anagram: the letters of ROUSE and NERO are rearranged; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Mistaken or incorrect; a synonym.

clue.text: Tweedledum's poisonous epithet for Tweedledee?

parts.note: in Through the Looking-Glass one twin is furious that the other spoilt his new toy noisemaker

explanation.surface: One twin calls the other a venomous name.
explanation.walkthrough: Tweedledum's quarrel is over his 'nice new rattle', so the brother who broke it is a rattle snake.
explanation.definitionFit: A venomous American viper with a noisy tail, and a fit insult for whoever broke the toy.

clue.text: Always giving consent

explanation.surface: Someone who says yes every time.
explanation.definitionFit: An old word for ever or forever, and a voting word meaning yes.

clue.text: Smart dame in Holland's civic garb ?

definitions.text: Smart dame in Holland's civic garb

indicators.note: a woman dressed in new clothes is rearranged, so her letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A well-dressed woman wears the city costume of the Netherlands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in ... garb' dresses up the letters of SMART DAME, rearranging them into the Dutch capital, which is also what the clue as a whole describes.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital city of the Netherlands, often called Holland.

clue.text: The best form of government?

parts.note: the Greek root aristos means best, so this is rule by the best people

explanation.surface: Someone asks which political system is ideal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'best' sounds like a judgment, but it translates the Greek root of the word: government by the best (the nobility).
explanation.definitionFit: Rule by a noble elite, from Greek words for best and power.

clue.text: The cause of many pre-death deaths, said Caesar

definitions.text: The cause of many pre-death deaths, said Caesar

parts.words: The cause of many pre-death deaths, said Caesar
parts.note: Shakespeare's Caesar says cowards die many times before their deaths

explanation.surface: A Roman general names what kills people before they die.
explanation.walkthrough: In Julius Caesar the line is 'Cowards die many times before their deaths; the valiant never taste of death but once.'
explanation.definitionFit: Lack of courage, which by Caesar's saying makes a person die repeatedly in imagination.

clue.text: Woman in medical jurisprudence ?

parts.note: a nurse (a sister, in British hospitals) who works in the law

explanation.surface: A female expert on medical law.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a senior nurse is called a sister, so a medical woman in law is a 'sister in law'.
explanation.definitionFit: A relation by marriage: a spouse's female sibling or a sibling's wife.

clue.text: "I am forbid To tell the —— of my prison-house" (Hamlet)

definitions.text: "I am forbid To tell the —— of my prison-house" (Hamlet)

parts.words: "I am forbid To tell the —— of my prison-house" (Hamlet)
parts.note: the Ghost of Hamlet's father may not reveal what lies hidden in purgatory

explanation.surface: A line from the Ghost's speech in Hamlet with a word missing.
explanation.definitionFit: Hidden things that must not be told, which the Ghost is barred from revealing.

clue.text: Stamp? The last thing to do!

explanation.surface: Franking a letter is the final chore.
explanation.definitionFit: A die is a tool for stamping coins or seals, and dying is everyone's final act.

clue.text: Game in which top spin is devilish important

definitions.text: Game in which top spin is devilish important

parts.words: Game in which top spin is devilish important
parts.note: a juggling toy spun on a string, its name from the Italian for devil

explanation.surface: A sport where putting topspin on the ball matters hugely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top spin' suggests tennis, but the toy is a two-headed spinning top whirled on a string, and its name comes from the Italian word for devil.
explanation.definitionFit: A juggling game spinning a double-cone top on a cord between two sticks.

clue.text: Life's refugees ?

parts.note: people who flee everyday reality as refugees flee danger

explanation.surface: People who have fled their whole existence.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who retreat into fantasy to avoid harsh reality.

clue.text: Conceited people to come to grips with

indicators.note: the letters come to, or arrive at, a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Smug people we must learn to deal with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'come to' rearranges GRIPS; 'to' and 'with' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Self-righteous, smugly superior people.

clue.text: They're not prefixed "B" in Norfolk only

definitions.text: They're not prefixed "B" in Norfolk only

parts.words: They're not prefixed "B" in Norfolk only
parts.note: in Norfolk a B in front makes the ..., the county's lakes and waterways; elsewhere these routes need no letter

explanation.surface: Highway names lacking a B classification exist only in one county.
explanation.walkthrough: 'B' suggests British B-class highways, but the Norfolk Broads are a waterway region in eastern England; drop the B and you have highways everywhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Highways and streets; with a B in front they become Norfolk's Broads.

clue.text: At this rate Veronica is well off

indicators.note: one word is off, taken away from the plant's name

parts.note: Veronica is the botanical name of the speedwell, a small blue flower
taken as written

explanation.surface: Seen this way, a woman called Veronica is wealthy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Veronica' looks like a woman's name but is the plant genus; 'is well off' says that word is removed from its common name, and 'At this' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Velocity or pace; a synonym.

clue.text: There are a couple of Scottish banks in this district

definitions.text: There are a couple of Scottish banks in this district

parts.words: There are a couple of Scottish banks in this district
parts.note: banks read as financial firms, but they are the two sides of a Scottish river

explanation.surface: Two Scottish financial houses have branches in this area.
explanation.walkthrough: The Dee is a river in Aberdeenshire, Scotland; its two sides are its banks.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scottish region along the river Dee, its name meaning that river's side.

clue.text: A literally sound measure

indicators.note: a sound is something spoken, so the letter is said aloud

parts.note: literally read as 'by letter': the letter L

explanation.surface: A truly reasonable unit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'literally' means 'of letters'; the letter L, spoken, is the old cloth length.
explanation.definitionFit: An old English unit of length, about 45 inches, for cloth.

clue.text: Poe said to be uncommonly fat

indicators.note: done uncommonly, in an unusual way, so the letters are put in an unusual order

explanation.surface: Edgar Allan Poe is reported to have been very overweight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uncommonly' rearranges POE and SAID; 'to be' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Fatty, relating to animal fat stored in the body; a technical synonym.

clue.text: Request in writing for concealment

definitions.note: a noun; the answer is a plural noun for things used to hide faces

indicators.note: one piece is placed in the other, inside its letters

parts.note: MS is the abbreviation for manuscript, a piece of writing
to request is to ask

explanation.surface: A written application asking to keep something secret.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts ASK inside MS.
explanation.definitionFit: Disguises worn over the face serve to hide identity.

clue.text: A Belgian nobleman ?

parts.note: a peer from the Belgian city of Liège

explanation.surface: An aristocrat from Belgium.
explanation.walkthrough: Liège is a Belgian city, so its lord is the feudal superior whose vassals owe him allegiance.
explanation.definitionFit: A feudal superior to whom a vassal owes service and loyalty.
